official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be from a non-European Union state and their household must not file taxes within the European Union. Sciences Po takes into account the tax residence of the parents, not of the student; students whose parents have a tax residence in the EU cannot apply, unless they are eligible for financial independence.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship exists 'in order to welcome the very best international students from outside the European Union'.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field restriction, but restricted by programme: the Undergraduate College or a two-year Master's programme, excluding the Joint Master's in Journalism and International Affairs, the Master's in journalism and the other programmes listed under eligibility.
official.duration: Bachelor's: tuition-fee grant for the first year of studies, retained during the third year abroad; adjusted each year in line with any increase in tuition fees. Master's: EUR 18,500 tuition-fee exemption for each of the two years of the programme.
official.description: Sciences Po created the Emile Boutmy scholarship, named after the founder of the school (1872), in order to welcome the very best international students from outside the European Union. It is a tuition-fee exemption awarded to admitted first-time applicants of the Undergraduate College and the two-year Master's programmes, funded with the support of private sponsors such as the Chalhoub Group, Fondation Genevieve McMillan-Reba Stewart, L'Oreal and Michel David-Weill.
official.region: France - Paris campus and the regional campuses (Dijon, Le Havre, Menton, Nancy, Poitiers, Reims)
official.program_type: Merit-based tuition-fee exemption for admitted first-time international students of the Undergraduate College and the two-year Master's programmes
official.english_requirement: The scholarship page publishes no minimum score: language requirements depend on the programme applied for, and test results, when needed, must be attached directly into the online application before the programme deadline. Applicants who studied at least two consecutive years within the same degree-granting university programme fully taught in English are exempted from the English test. For the 2027 intake, language tests must have been taken on 1 January 2025 or later; Cambridge certificates have lifetime validity.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a tuition-fee waiver, not a living grant: even a full exemption leaves you funding housing, food, health cover and flights in Paris out of pocket, and Sciences Po states plainly that students who miss out must find another source of funding. Your one and only shot is the admission application itself - tick the Emile Boutmy box in the 'Financial information' section before you submit, because nothing can be added afterwards and no post-admission request is accepted. The most common silent disqualifier is the household tax-residence test, which follows your parents' tax residence rather than yours, so EU-taxpaying parents end the application no matter where you personally live or study.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU applicants from households with no EU tax residence who have an outstanding secondary or undergraduate record and are applying to the Sciences Po Undergraduate College or a two-year Master's.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your parents' tax residence is outside the EU before you build the application; if it is inside the EU, the Boutmy route is closed and you should look at CROUS-scale or external funding instead
Check your target programme against the exclusion list (journalism Master's, one-year Master's, most dual degrees, Ph.D., French graduate procedure) before spending the EUR 150 fee
Tick the Emile Boutmy box in the 'Financial information' section, then re-open the file to verify it registered before you press submit
Book any required language test early enough that the result is inside the two-year validity window and uploaded before the programme deadline
Line up the two academic referees first - an undergraduate file without both references is incomplete and is not assessed
Prepare the Financial information section evidence (household income and tax documents) in the same session, since the file must be complete on submission
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the application without declaring the scholarship - the box is easy to miss and it cannot be ticked later
Household tax residence inside the EU, including a dual EU citizenship or Quebec residency at Master's level
Being an exchange student, a current Sciences Po student, or a deferred candidate - all three are barred outright
A weak admissions file: the scholarship is decided inside admissions review, so a file that only just clears the admission bar rarely attracts an award
Switching programme after admission - enrolling in a dual degree in the third year forfeits the award
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award covers tuition only. You still fund the EUR 150 non-refundable application fee, housing, food, local transport, health cover, visa and residence-permit costs, and return travel. Sciences Po publishes a budget page and a tuition-fees and scholarships guide for these figures.
document_audit: Every PDF must be under 2 MB and named in English or French - oversized or misnamed uploads are a routine cause of incomplete files
Scan the three transcripts of each academic year into a single chronological PDF as Sciences Po explicitly asks
Do not attach documents upside down, and check the orientation after scanning
Referees get a few extra days after your submission, but the responsibility for chasing them is yours - send reminders through the candidate space
If admitted and awarded, you must declare yourself a scholarship holder in step 2 and upload the dated, signed certificate in step 5 of administrative registration
alerts: Deadline trap: the undergraduate scholarship deadline (13 January 2027) is earlier than the final undergraduate application date of 1 March 2027, so a late-round applicant is automatically out
Once submitted, the application can no longer be modified and no later documents are considered - completeness at the moment of submission is what counts
Accept the admission offer while waiting for the scholarship decision; a deferral requested before the grant decision kills any chance of applying again

The Boutmy award cannot be stacked with another Sciences Po or partner scholarship (Mastercard, CARE, Fondation de France/Rene Seydoux, China Scholarship Council), but it can sit alongside Eiffel, AEFE or French government awards
Failing to validate the academic year forfeits the scholarship
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create the account at admission.sciencespo.fr, complete the application including the 'Financial information' declaration of the Boutmy scholarship, pay the fee, click 'Submit my application' before the deadline, then wait for the admission decision first and the scholarship decision afterwards.

The Master in Management application deadlines are 7 October 2026, 26 November 2026, 17 February 2027 and 28 April 2027, all at 12pm. MBA scholarships run parallel to the rolling MBA application deadlines for the January and September intakes, with decisions within five weeks of the application deadline.

official.description: HEC Paris offers two types of scholarships for international applicants to its Master's programmes and MBA: merit-based awards, considered automatically for admitted students and decided on academic excellence, application strength, interview performance and GMAT/GRE/TAGE-MAGE results, and need-based awards, applied for through the Applicant Space and granted within defined nationalities and profiles. All of them are paid as a tuition-fee reduction rather than a cash grant.
official.program_type: Merit-based and need-based tuition-fee reduction scholarships for HEC Paris Master's programmes and the MBA
official.english_requirement: 'All candidates are required to submit proof of English language proficiency' by uploading scores for the TOEIC (all four parts), TOEFL, IELTS ibt or Cambridge exam. Tests are waived for English natives, who upload a scanned copy of the first page of their passport, and for candidates who completed their entire degree taught in English, who upload a statement of language of instruction issued by their university. No minimum score is published.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no single HEC Paris scholarship here - there are roughly a dozen, and the route you take depends entirely on which one you are chasing. If you hold a non-French diploma you are already in the running for the Foundation Excellence award with nothing to do, because admitted students are screened automatically, but every need-based award requires you to submit the Master's application first and then file a separate form in the Applicant Space by noon on your round date. Treat the round you choose as a funding decision, not just an admissions one: the Eiffel nomination and the Lafayette Fellowship are only open to Round 1 and Round 2 applicants, and the 30% Club award is only live in Round 2.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International applicants with a non-French degree and a strong GMAT/GRE or TAGE-MAGE score who can either document limited financial means or fit one of the nationality, gender or field profiles HEC funds.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit the initial Master's application before anything else - the need-based form is gated behind it and cannot be started earlier
Map yourself against the named awards before choosing a round, since several are round-locked (Eiffel Round 1 only, 30% Club Round 2, Lafayette Rounds 1-2)

Draft the 350-word essay early: VOLKSWAGEN wants an automotive-industry motivation, Future Leaders of Africa wants your view of the continent's challenges, and Imagine Fellowship asks about Business & Peace
Gather income evidence for the need-based jury, plus a parents' income document and sports licence if the Stan Schwab award applies to you
For Women in Finance & Technology as a non-native French speaker, book a DALF, TCF or TEF at C1-C2 and email the score to scholarships@hec.fr
MBA applicants: reserve the final essay of the application for anything the Excellence and Diversity committees should know, since that is where they look
common_rejection_risks: Filing the needs-based form even one minute past noon on the round deadline - the cut-off is absolute and forms completed later are not considered
Holding a French diploma or French dual nationality, which rules out most merit awards and the Equal Opportunity Scholarship entirely
Applying for Forte or MBA Excellence while an employer or government sponsors more than half your tuition
Being already enrolled in France and applying for the Equal Opportunity Scholarship
Overstating financial circumstances - HEC warns that any bursary is automatically suspended if information proves false
Counting on an Eiffel or Lafayette award as your fee solution: Eiffel explicitly does not pay tuition fees
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The awards reduce tuition only, so you still fund the EUR 180 non-refundable Master's application fee, housing in the Paris area, food, transport, health cover, visa costs and flights. MBA Laidlaw recipients are told to expect roughly EUR 25,000 of living expenses over a 16-month programme on top of the full-tuition award.
document_audit: The 350-word essays must arrive as PDFs at scholarships@hec.fr, on the day the admissibility results are published for your round - a late email is a lost award
The Garzouzi clean criminal record is a separate PDF emailed to scholarships@hec.fr, not an upload in the form
English proficiency waivers need evidence, not assertion: passport first page for natives, or an official language-of-instruction statement for a fully English-taught degree
Official test scores must be sent through mba.com (GMAT/GMAT Focus) or ETS with code 3623 (GRE) in addition to the uploaded screenshot
Referees should be approached at least four weeks before the round deadline, since the confidential reference must be in the portal by then
alerts: The need-based deadline is noon Paris time on the round date, which is the same day the admissibility results are published - plan for a compressed window
Scholarship results and amounts are final, and decisions arrive by email within a week of the admission results, so you may be deciding on other funding with very little notice
Conflicting sponsorship rules: CMA-CGM can be combined with HEC Excellence and Diversity, but Laidlaw voids any other HEC scholarship, and Sanofi is not cumulative with other HEC Foundation awards
On the MBA the combined HEC Excellence, Forte Foundation, ARD and Paris Saclay awards cannot exceed 50% of tuition fees, and double-degree awards are pro-rated
Recommitting to a second year of the Garzouzi award requires a 3.5 GPA in M1 plus fresh foundation approval, not automatic renewal
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: File the HEC Master's or MBA application by the round deadline, wait for the admissibility email, then file the Needs-Based Scholarship Form in the Applicant Space by noon that day and email any award-specific PDF to scholarships@hec.fr; merit awards are decided without any action from you.
